These appeals coming on for Hearing,
through physical hearing/video conference, this day T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA, J., delivered the following:
C/w MFA No.201660/2016  4  JUDGMENT

In these appeals, the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 31.03.2016 passed in MVC No.1954/2014 on the file of the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT-XIII,
Vijayapura (Hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short)
2. MFA No.201710/2016 has been filed by the petitioners seeking enhancement of the compensation and the connected appeal, MFA No.201660/2016 has been filed by the 2nd respondent - Insurance Company challenging the quantum of compensation.
3.
The parties will be referred as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
4. Briefly stated, the facts are that, one Umakanth Shankar Chati is the son of the petitioners, who is the husband of Smt. Aishwarya, the deceased.
Six days prior to 07.04.2014, their marriage was solemnized.

On 07.04.2014 Umakanth while driving the car bearing No.MH-13/AZ-7798 along with the deceased, near Barshi-Yedshi Road near Ganesh Dabha, met with an accident in which the latter was killed at the spot.
5. The petitioners being in-laws of the deceased claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- before the Tribunal.
They pleaded that the deceased was II year Engineering student and also doing private services earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company on the ground that the petitioners are not the Class-1 heirs of the deceased and they are not dependents.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.6,51,000/- with interest at 6% per annum.
6. The petitioners have pleaded inadequacy in the compensation.

Insurance Company has contended that the petitioners are not the Class-1 heirs, marriage of the deceased took place with their son just 6 days prior to the accident, the deceased was a student, her husband is alive and the claim is not maintainable.

sentences.text:
According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, the deceased was though Engineering student, earning by doing part time job, the petitioners are the dependents, future prospects was not considered and accordingly he sought for re- assessment and enhancement of compensation.
8.
Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contended that the petitioners are the in- laws of the deceased.
Within 6 days of the marriage, deceased was killed in the accident, tort feasor was her own husband, against whom the criminal prosecution was hoisted.
Since, he himself was a tort feasor he was not entitled to claim compensation and for this reason he set up his parents as dependents to claim compensation, which is not permissible.
9. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records in both the appeals.

10. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, death of the deceased in the accident,
the relationship between the deceased with the petitioners.
The material on record would point out that at the time of accident, husband of the deceased was the driver of the car.
It is specifically alleged against him that he drove the car in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree killing his own wife at the spot.
The husband of the deceased is alive and he is the legal Class-I heir of the deceased.

When he is alive, by keeping him away, whether the in-laws can claim the compensation is the precise point for consideration in these two appeals apart from whether the just compensation was awarded by the Tribunal.
If the in- laws are considered as legal representatives within the meaning of Section 166 of M.V. Act, in presence of their son, then the question of enhancement arises.

11. Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in N.
Jayasree and Others Versus Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 967 and submitted that in view of the law laid down, mother-in-law is the dependent and therefore, the petition is maintainable and submitted this Court to proceed to enhance the compensation.

entities.text:
N.
Jayasree and Others Versus Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 967
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In the above judgment the Hon'ble Apex Court held that in order to maintain a claim petition, it is sufficient for the claimant to establish his dependency on the deceased.
Section 166 of MV Act makes it clear that every legal representatives who suffers on account of the death of a person in motorcycle accident should have a remedy for realization of compensation.

At Para Nos.16 and 21 of its judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"16.
We are also of the view that in order to maintain a claim petition, it is sufficient for the claimant to establish his loss of dependency.

Section 166 of the MV Act makes it clear that every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person in a motor vehicle accident should have a remedy for realization of compensation".
"21. Coming to the facts of the present case, the fourth appellant was the mother-in-law of the deceased.
Materials on record clearly establish that she was residing with the deceased and his family members.

She was dependent on him for Shankarrao And Anr vs Prabhuling And Anr on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92629343/
4

sentences.text: her shelter and maintenance.
It is not uncommon in Indian Society for the mother-in-law to live with her daughter and son-in-law during her old age and be dependent upon her son-in-- law for her maintenance.
Appellant No.4 herein may not be a legal heir of the deceased, but she certainly suffered on account of his death.

Therefore, we have no hesitation to hold that she is a "legal representative" under Section 166 of the MV Act and is entitled to maintain a claim petition."
13.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the facts of the said case and facts of the case on hand are different and therefore, petitioners cannot be treated as dependents.

14. We have carefully perused the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court wherein the facts were that 52 years old Assistant Professor of Mathematics died in an accident; a claim was made by his wife and children and mother-in-law also joined as dependent of son-in-law.

The Hon'ble Apex Court held that it is not uncommon in Indian society for the mother-in-law to live with her daughter and son-in-law during her old age and be dependent on her son-in-law for her maintenance and therefore, held that mother-in-law is also dependent on son-in-law to claim compensation within the meaning of Section 166 of MV Act.
15.
Herein this case, no doubt the petitioners are parents-in-law of the deceased and the deceased came to the house of the petitioners just 6 days prior to the accident.
The accident was caused by their own son who is alive and he is the legal representative of the deceased.
The facts of this case is not identical to the case dealt with by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
The husband of the deceased is very much alive and he is outside the Tribunal watching the proceedings asking his parents to claim the compensation as dependents.
The petitioners are claiming that they are legal representatives and dependents on their student daughter-in-law who entered their house 6 days prior to the accident.
Therefore, the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court is not helpful to the facts of this case.
16. The deceased was admittedly an Engineering student, not earning and therefore, the petitioners have to establish that they are dependants on the deceased.
As stated supra they have no legal rights to assert that they are the dependents when her husband is very much alive, who is legally disabled from claiming compensation as tort-feaser.

Therefore, the petitioners will not get any right to claim compensation under Section 166 of MV Act.
17.

In the result, the following:
ORDER
The appeal by the petitioners in MFA No.201710/2016 for enhancement of compensation is dismissed.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company in MFA No.201660/2016 is allowed.
Consequently, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners stands dismissed.
